title: The Minor Law Books: Nârada and Brihaspati
altTitles: Sacred Books of the East, vol. 33
attributionNote: The treatises are ascribed to the sages Narada and Brihaspati. Both are anonymous compilations of earlier legal material, and the Brihaspati text survives only in the form reconstructed by its editors.
description: The Minor Law Books present the classical Hindu law of procedure. Narada, in eighteen chapters, is almost entirely concerned with courts and disputes: the judge and the assessors, plaints and answers, the burden of proof, documents, witnesses, ordeals, and the law of deposit, loans, partnership, wages, sale, boundaries, defamation and assault. Brihaspati, recovered fragmentarily, covers the same ground and adds a distinctive treatise on the duties of the king and the administration of justice.
historicalContext: Narada and Brihaspati belong to the later smriti period, when the legal process itself rather than ritual duty became the central subject of the texts. Julius Jolly translated them in 1889 as SBE 33; his introduction reconstructs the relation between the two treatises and the earlier schools.
availabilityNote: Complete as published. Narada's eighteen chapters and the recovered text of Brihaspati are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed chapter per chapter. The volume's introduction, abbreviations and addenda are not part of the work.
